source.title: Adjoint Inversion Reveals Holographic Superposition and Destructive Interference in CNN Classifiers

page_placements.theme: Local semantic regions and vision reconstruction geometry

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports results on shared scene content in CNN channel inversions and their signed recombination, but does not test the claim versions about sparse overcomplete feature storage, capacity-driven polysemanticity, LLM representations, SAE features, or the dimensionality of underlying model features.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition and describes its image-space findings as related to the broader superposition perspective. Its own measurements concern input-conditioned pixel-space channel inversions, not whether sparse features outnumber representational dimensions or how such features are stored. The paper also reports CNN and ViT signed-reconstruction outcomes; these concern image-space recombination rather than any listed version. Cited results from other work were not extracted.
record.test_reason: The paper uses 'shared-scene superposition' for a pixel-space finding: CNN channel inversions share a common scene component plus channel-specific residuals. It cites Toy Models of Superposition only as a 'broader superposition perspective'. It never varies sparsity or feature count against dimension. It never measures polysemanticity or capacity competition. It does not study LLMs or SAEs, and it does not test the dimensionality of model features. Its rows measure inversion spectra, foreground energy of signed recombinations, and channel-selection accuracy, which are constructs different from every listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors also claim that region-ranked channel ablations link inversion preferences to class predictions, and that CovVol channel selection helps under extreme compression and corruption. Neither result bears on the claim versions.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses input-conditioned adjoint inversions with learned per-plane scalar calibration, spectral analysis, and signed channel recombination. It does not implement the sparse toy-network method or test its feature-count and sparsity conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: The signed-reconstruction foreground-energy gain is reported for the CNN experiments but not for the pure ViT-B/16/Pets setting. In the spectral analysis, channel-centering sharply reduces leading-mode fractions.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-image uncentered leading-mode energy of deep-channel inversions far exceeds matched nulls: 0.774 on CUB/ConvNeXt-B and 0.959 on Pets/ResNet-50. Channel-centering removes most of this: CUB falls to null level and Pets stays modestly above it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual CNN channel inversions share a dominant input-aligned scene component plus channel-specific residuals.

fits_no_version.finding: Signed classifier-weighted sums of channel inversions concentrate foreground energy beyond either sign-restricted component in four CNNs (0.722 vs 0.425 on CUB/ConvNeXt-B). No such gain appears in ViT-B/16 on Pets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-weighted recombination cancels shared scene content in CNN inversions (destructive interference), and this effect does not transfer to the tested ViT.

record.problems: The spectral evidence in Table 8 is reported for two dataset-backbone pairs, and its quantities describe pixel-space inversions rather than latent feature units. The paper does not vary feature sparsity or feature count relative to representation dimensions. Several qualitative comparisons and the aggregate CNN/ViT signed-reconstruction contrast have no reported numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: CovVol compression and corruption results, CAM comparisons, and region-ranked channel ablations were not included because they do not directly measure the listed claim versions or the shared-scene inversion geometry. See Sections 3.2.4–3.4 and Supplementary C.6–C.8.

untested.parts: No toy model. No sparsity or feature-count versus dimension manipulation. No phase transition. No feature geometry.
Neither polysemantic neurons nor capacity allocation (dedicated vs shared dimensions) is measured.
No analysis of other causes of polysemanticity.
No LLMs and no SAE or dictionary recovery. The CNN channel-redundancy (pruning plateau) results are not feature-level evidence.
The rank-one shared component is a pixel-space direction across channel inversions. It does not show whether model features are 1-D or multi-dimensional.

record.verdict_notes: 'Superposition' here is a terminological borrowing for shared image content across channel inversions, not superposition of sparse features in activation space. The paper's only link to the original is one sentence calling its account 'related to the broader superposition perspective'. relation=discusses and tranche=T6 are appropriate.

versions.untested_parts: No test of sparse features exceeding dimensions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular feature geometry.
No test of polysemanticity, capacity competition, or dedicated versus shared dimensions.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity or whether polysemanticity evidences superposition.
No LLM feature-spread or SAE-recovery measurements.
No test of SAE features as complete, stable, or canonical units.
The paper measures a shared one-dimensional component in pixel-space channel inversions, but does not test whether the model's represented features are one-dimensional or multidimensional.

rows.subject: ResNet-18, ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, and ConvNeXt-Base
rows.operation_detail: Compared foreground energy in positive- and negative-weight class reconstructions with their signed sum.
rows.measure: Foreground energy proportion across sign components and full signed reconstruction
rows.baseline: Positive- and negative-weight components have similar foreground proportions
rows.value: The full signed sum has substantially higher foreground concentration; no exact values given for this aggregate statement.
rows.note: The paper summarizes the pattern across four ImageNet-pretrained backbones; the largest gain is stated to be for ConvNeXt-Base on both datasets.

rows.subject: ViT-B/16

rows.value: The full signed reconstruction does not show the foreground-energy gain observed in the CNN experiments.
rows.note: No numerical foreground-energy values are given.

relation.reason: Supplementary C.4 relates its image-space decomposition to the broader superposition perspective of Toy Models of Superposition without testing the catalog versions.

tranche.reason: The study measures shared scene content in calibrated pixel-space channel inversions, a different construct from V1–V6. It neither tests nor uses those claims as an established tool.

source_check.notes: All supplied numerical values, confidence intervals, and null baselines match the text. The rank-one-removal passage leaves its backbone and dataset unspecified; its statistics should remain unattached to a specific model.
